chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A woman sees purity, and she sees yellowness or some trace, so she does not know whether she has become pure or not. He said: “If that is so, then let her stand, press her stomach against a wall, and raise her leg upon a wall as you have seen a dog do when it wants to urinate; then she should insert cotton. If there is there blood even like the head of a fly, it will come out. If blood comes out, then she has not become pure; and if it does not come out, then she has become pure.”

This applies when it is within the range between the lesser number of menstrual days and the greater number of them. But if it exceeds ten, then if blood comes out, the days of her menstruation have ended according to what we have mentioned.

As for what he mentioned regarding the obligation of preceding ghusl with wudu, we have already explained earlier that no ghusl removes the obligation of wudu except ghusl of janabah, and what was mentioned there is sufficient, if Allah Most High wills. And what he mentioned concerning rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose is only sunnah (prophetic tradition); its mention has already passed in the chapter of taharah (ritual purity). And his statement regarding the order of ghusl has also already passed in the chapter of ghusl of janabah, and in it there is clarification and sufficiency, if Allah Most High wills, and it gives further clarification.

key_terms.الصُّفْرَةَ: yellowish discharge seen during or around menstruation
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: ritual purity, meaning the cessation of menstruation
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation as a legal state with specific rulings
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used for internal examination to detect blood
key_terms.الْمَضْمَضَةِ: rinsing the mouth as part of washing practices
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing for prayer

ai.seo_question: How does a woman determine whether she has become pure from menstruation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal method for determining whether a woman has become pure from menstruation when she sees uncertain signs such as yellowness or a slight trace. It also addresses related rulings on menstrual limits, wudu before ghusl, and notes that rinsing the mouth and nose in ghusl is sunnah (prophetic tradition), situating the discussion within the broader fiqh of taharah (ritual purity).
